claim: Experts debug faster and more accurately than novices on simple programs (LOGO, Pascal); the edge is hypothesis quality after less reading. Magnitudes in G&O unread (abstract only).
agent_test: Compare agent forced to state a ranked bug hypothesis after a capped read vs full read, equal tokens.

claim: Novices add new bugs while hunting the original; Vessey 1985 supports it: all 5 error-makers were chunk-classed novices, 8 mistakes (6 on the low-level bug), but classification is partly circular.
agent_test: Count regressions (new failing tests) per edit; cap edits per round and keep best-so-far.
note_d: LLM analogue: 11 of 22 confirmed-incorrect plausible patches were regressive (d12).

claim: Experts build a whole-system causal model early and search breadth-first; novices need more episodes (P=0.003, N=16).
agent_test: Require a system summary before first edit; compare to no summary.

claim: Chunking-based expertise class plus bug level explained 73.7% of debug time variance (experts 15m40s vs novices 28m03s, N=16); manager rating only 36.1% and 20m24s vs 23m19s.
agent_test: Not directly testable; shows labels by process are circular.

claim: No comprehension strategy gave best debugging in 75 novices; depth-first cluster fixed 1.00 of 4 bugs vs 1.65 and 2.00, with experience confounded (2.52, 1.20, 3.59).
agent_test: Randomise reading strategy across agent runs and test.

claim: Without an external signal, LLM self-correction does not help and often hurts: GPT-3.5 CSQA 75.8 -> 38.1; GSM8K 75.9 -> 74.7; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 -> 89.0 (verified).
agent_test: Equal-token: self-revise vs resample-and-vote vs external-checker revise.
boundary_note_d: Reasoning-tuned models show a small blind spot (d05) but o1-class models still overturn correct answers (d06). Not shown for 2026 models.
audit_note: Minor: the CSQA 75.8->38.1 and GSM8K 74.7 figures are rounds 1 and 2 respectively; Huang et al. attribute prior gains to oracle labels.

claim: Oracle labels inflate self-correction gains; some claimed gains came from weak first prompts.
agent_test: Always use well-formed first prompt in baseline.

claim: The LLM bottleneck is diagnosis not repair: human feedback raised GPT-4 repair 33.30 -> 52.60% (verified), stronger-model feedback helps a weaker coder; Tyen: mistake finding is weak (GPT-4 52.87) but repair given the location works.
agent_test: Split diagnosis from repair at equal tokens; give diagnosis more budget.
audit_note: Minor: 'diagnosis not repair' is a broad framing; human-feedback result is from 16 participants and 40 programs.

claim: At equal compute, self-repair gives little over resampling: GPT-4 APPS 10+1 = 1.05x, 2+10 = 0.97x; more initial samples always helped, more repairs marginal or negative.
agent_test: Spend tokens on N candidates vs repair rounds, fixed total.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Debugging effectiveness decays exponentially across attempts; most models lose 60-80% within 2-3 attempts; fresh start at decay point raised llama3.1:8b 72.56 -> 82.82 and deepseek-coder-v2 84.1 -> 92.1 (verified).
agent_test: Replicate on our model: restart with problem plus best-so-far after 2 failed rounds.
note_d: CodeMonkeys (d08) supports fresh starts at equal cost but is not a replication of the decay result.

claim: A syntax linter guard on edits raises resolve rate 15.0 -> 18.0% (SWE-bench Lite); 51.7% of trajectories had a failed edit; recovery 90.5% from any attempt but 57.2% after one failed edit (verified).
agent_test: Reject edits that break checks; measure regressions.

claim: Keeping fewer observations (last 5) and summarised search match or beat full history in SWE-agent (18.0 vs 15.0).
agent_test: Compare full vs trimmed history at equal tokens.

claim: A fixed localise-repair-validate pipeline with test-based patch selection is competitive with open agents: 32.00% at $0.70; reproduction tests lifted 25.67 -> 32.00%.
agent_test: Fixed pipeline vs free-form agent at equal tokens.

claim: Self-debug gains are largest with unit-test execution feedback (up to +12 on TransCoder and MBPP), while without execution plain pass/fail feedback can hurt (Codex MBPP 61.4 -> 57.6) but code explanation or trace feedback still helps (Codex MBPP 64.4 and 66.2; Spider +2-3%).
agent_test: Ablate tests/execution feedback in the loop.
audit_note: Chen et al. show self-debug also helps without execution when the model explains its code (Spider +2-3%, MBPP Codex 61.4 -> 64.4 with explanation, 66.2 with trace); only simple yes/no feedback hurt (Codex MBPP 57.6), so execution feedback is not the sole driver.
claim_before_audit: Execution feedback is what makes self-debug work: up to +12 with unit tests, but without them simple feedback can hurt (Codex MBPP 61.4 -> 57.6).

claim: Self-Refine gains are large on weak models but near zero for strong models on code (GPT-4 92.9 -> 93.1).
agent_test: Check gain by base strength.

claim: Models do worse as bug count rises: GPT-4 DebugBench 93.6 missing colons, 73.1 condition, double 70.7, triple 58.9, quadruple 55.9; runtime feedback helps syntax not logic bugs.
agent_test: Fix one bug at a time vs all at once.

claim: LLMs reviewing novice code find a real issue 90% of the time (GPT-3.5) but invent non-existent issues 40%.
agent_test: Require reproducing evidence for any claimed bug.

claim: Redoing a step at a wrong location hurts correct traces (word sorting 11.11% of correct traces broken); a locator helps once accuracy is about 60-70%.
agent_test: Edit only when a located error is verified.

claim: Models fix an error they would miss in their own output when it is presented as someone else's: 64.5% average blind spot over 14 open non-reasoning models; 'Wait' cuts it 89.3%; reasoning models show little.
agent_test: Present the model's own draft as a third party's patch to review; compare with and without a 'Wait' cue.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction still overturns correct answers in o1-class models (o1-mini 34.0%, o1-preview 15.6% on Yes/No QA).
agent_test: Re-run on current models with and without an external check.

claim: Reading every file is affordable if shared across many edits (scan under 15% of cost, 92.6% recall at 128k); then rank to about 75k tokens (50.5x cut). This does not test capped versus full reading at equal tokens.
agent_test: Equal-token test: capped read plus forced ranked hypothesis versus full read.

claim: System-level localization quality tracks resolution: six SWE-bench Verified systems rank the same by file-level F1 and by resolved count (one exception).
agent_test: Score hypothesis quality blind per trace and correlate with fix rate.

claim: Passing tests overstates fix quality: 7.8% of plausible patches fail the full developer tests, 29.6% differ from the gold patch, inflation 6.4 points; 36 under-tested instances and 345 wrong patches found elsewhere.
agent_test: Run pass-to-pass tests plus differential checks before keeping a patch.

claim: Agent failures are mostly looping on a failed strategy (flawed reasoning is the top root cause); pipeline tools fail at localization (51.3% of Agentless failures).
agent_test: Force a new hypothesis after a failed round.

claim: A same-model supervisory reviewer resolved 24 of 108 tasks (22.2%) that the baseline had failed; no matched-compute control seen.
agent_test: Compare reviewer against equal-token resampling.

claim: Block-level runtime state (LDB) improves debugging over whole-program feedback: GPT-3.5 HumanEval 73.8 to 82.9 (+9.1) against Self-Debug +7.3.
agent_test: Ablate variable-trace feedback.
